memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses led the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at
the foot of the mountain. Mount Sinai was covered with smoke, because the LORD
descended on it in fire. The smoke billowed up from it like smoke from a furnace,
and the whole mountain trembled violently." - Ex 19:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the small phrase: "Moses led the people out of the camp to meet with
God."

They could have stayed inside. Everything about the scene said stay away, and
God had drawn a boundary line. Yet Moses led them out, and they came and stood
at the foot of the mountain.

That took courage. But it is what they were made for. God had brought them out of
Egypt "to myself" (v.4), and here they are, standing as close as they are
permitted to stand.

Then the mountain itself reacts. Smoke like a furnace, fire, and the whole mass
of rock trembling violently. Even creation cannot stay steady in the presence of
its Maker.

Scripture uses this scene later to make a point about what lasts. "At that time
his voice shook the earth, but now he has promised, 'Once more I will shake not
only the earth but also the heavens'" (Heb 12:26). The writer's conclusion is
that we are receiving "a kingdom that cannot be shaken" (Heb 12:28).

Everything that can be shaken eventually will be. What remains is what God gives.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your life is built on something that can be shaken?
2. Are you moving toward God or keeping a comfortable distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, shake loose whatever I have built on unstable ground. Hold me in what
cannot be shaken. Amen.
